scope: Eighth expansion batch: 24 exercises on purposes, causes and alternatives. Three tame-purpose and six tame-cause items; three each for sincere okage credit, literal sei blame, kawari substitution, tsuide secondary errands and kawari compensating trade-offs. Scope is the stated functions, not every beneficiary, irony, exchange or causal construction.

sources.section: Purpose tame ni: goal, nonpast verb and noun + no attachment. This is the purpose page, distinct from the separate causal slug /ために.

Causal tame ni: inspected explanation and raw Structure metadata. Verb, i-adjective, na-adjective + na and noun + no attachment; examples include a present adjective cause and a favorable result. Past verbs are frequent, not obligatory; ni may be omitted in suitable causal formulations.
Appreciative attribution, attributive attachment and explicit caution that okage can also be sarcastic. Literal use is specified in the questions.
Unwanted-result attribution and attributive attachment; identifies the spelling 所為 with reading sei.
Substitution, attributive attachment and the alternative spelling 替わり alongside 代わり.

sources.publisher: Shogakukan, Seisenban Nihon Kokugo Daijiten via Kotobank
sources.section: The NOUN kawari entry, not Daijisen's gawari suffix entry on the same page: section one, senses 1-2 for replacement/representation and sense 3(i) for an exchange or corresponding compensation, usually with an adnominal modifier and ni. Spellings 代/替 are distinguished from section two's change senses.

Substitution or Trade and The Compensating Sense: separates replacement, an exchange of actions and an advantage offsetting a disadvantage. Supplementary teaching source, used alongside the dictionary noun sense.
Using a main activity as the occasion for a secondary task, verb/noun attachment and 序で spelling. Does not make habitual use or a gap between tasks categorically invalid.

Reviewer inspected the actual API response: noun 序で／序, both read ついで, and adverb 序でに／序に support the two kanji spellings for the accompanying-opportunity use. Accept 序 as the literal blank before printed に; this does not license 次いで, a different sequencing expression.

authoringNotes: All scenarios are newly authored, not copied source exercises. Exact sentences, accepted spellings and distractors require independent linguistic review.

The six purpose/completed-cause items visibly request only dictionary or ta forms of a supplied verb before printed tame ni. Their context fixes the actual event status. Other tame-cause items use present adjectives, preventing a false rule that causal tame always needs a past verb.

Credit/blame questions visibly restrict the answer to okage or sei and expressly exclude sarcasm. The rain pair prevents assuming a cause has a fixed positive or negative value independent of the result.

Substitution/secondary-errand items visibly request kawari or tsuide. The main task is explicitly canceled/replaced or actually performed with an additional task. The library item explicitly excludes payment/exchange as the intended relationship.

Cause/trade-off items visibly request tame or kawari and explicitly select causation or compensating comparison. Quiet surroundings give a favorable causal result; trade-offs run both from drawback to advantage and advantage to drawback.

All option labels and accepted strings are literal missing spans. Printed ni/de and connectors remain outside the blanks. Usual kanji and kana variants are accepted, while kana remains the default model for the grammatical nouns.

Screen the full article inventory: neutral tame overlaps with evaluated okage/sei causes; よう can also express desired outcomes in suitable purpose formulations; toki/ori/sai locate occasions without necessarily adding a secondary-errand relation; ue and wari can describe other relations between features. Restrict visibly rather than falsely reject otherwise natural whole-sentence alternatives.

All earlier 95 exercise records remain unchanged. One SRS identity per new exercise, not per answer spelling or presentation. These controlled tasks do not establish unrestricted mastery of all cause, purpose and contrast expressions.
